reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistently no redline or comment was produced — the rendered text is identical to the original paragraphs, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to assess.

Substantively correct classification: the rule constrains Vendor audit rights running against us, and the cited excerpts (Section 3 restrictions ending at limb (g) with use covenants only; Section 17(b) self-certification of destruction/return) show no inspection, verification, records or system-access right in Garman's favour. Absence of any audit right is better than the preferred position on every parameter (frequency, notice, cost, system access).

Inserting audit parameters where no audit right exists would create new Vendor entitlements and increase our exposure; declining to redline is the smallest-edit outcome and the correct playbook treatment.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a heuristic false signal here — the regex has no audit clause to match — and the rationale correctly identifies and explains that.

Section 16 escrow examination and Section 17(b) certification are properly distinguished: the former runs in our favour and the latter involves no Garman entry, inspection or system access, so neither engages this rule.
